query: High-entropy alloys can combine mechanical strength, wear resistance, corrosion protection, oxidation resistance, and thermal stability, while their large compositional space offers opportunities to tune degradation in harsh environments. Prior studies have largely considered wear and corrosion separately, and only a few reports address their combined action, leaving the governing behavior poorly understood. For a high-entropy alloy subjected to tribo-corrosion, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs the coupled response and why? Describe a controlled comparison that would isolate the governing cause, predict changes in total degradation and its wear and corrosion components relative to a matched baseline, state where the prediction should hold or fail, connect it to the available prior evidence, and identify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The coupled tribo‐corrosion behavior of a high‐entropy alloy is governed by the kinetics and mechanical integrity of its passive oxide film under sliding.  Enhancing passivation via minor Al alloying (forming a stable Al₂O₃‐enriched film) will suppress both wear‐accelerated corrosion and mechanical removal by maintaining a self‐healing protective layer.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA disc, mirror‐polished, air‐passivated
generation.intervention: Add 5 at% Al to form (CoCrFeMnNi)₉₅Al₅ HEA
generation.conditions: Reciprocating sliding against an Al₂O₃ ball in 3.5 wt% NaCl at 25 °C, 5 N normal load, 1 Hz, 10 000 cycles
generation.structural_mediator: Thickness, composition, and adhesion of the Al₂O₃‐enriched passive film
generation.mechanism: Al promotes rapid formation and repair of a mechanically robust Al₂O₃‐rich oxide layer under wear, reducing exposure of fresh metal and thus limiting both mechanical wear and localized corrosion
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi baseline, the Al‐doped HEA will show a substantial decrease in total mass loss (≈ 30%–50%), a reduction in wear volume (≈ 30%–40%), and lower steady‐state corrosion current (≈ 50% reduction), indicating diminished wear–corrosion synergy
generation.baseline: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi under identical tribo-corrosion test
generation.boundary: Holds in near‐neutral chloride environments and moderate sliding loads (< 10 N) where passive‐film regeneration can compete with its removal; fails under extreme loads or purely abrasive (nonoxidizing) conditions where the film cannot reform
generation.uncertainty: Exact magnitude of improvement depends on Al content and test parameters; regeneration kinetics under dynamic sliding are not yet quantified

falsification_experiment.design: Perform paired tribo‐corrosion tests on CoCrFeMnNi and (CoCrFeMnNi)₉₅Al₅ under the stated conditions.  Monitor in situ passive‐film growth by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), then measure wear volume, total mass loss, and corrosion current.  Analyze post‐test film thickness/composition by TEM/EDS.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-doped HEA does not exhibit reduced total mass loss, wear volume, or corrosion current, or if no enhancement in passive‐film formation/repair is observed compared to baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
